learning: Iterations 7 to 10 show that lowering yaw inertia through mass and body_length raised slalom progress (0.30 to 0.76) and finishes (0 to 6/20) while the s-bend and oval held. Wheel_track 0.09 m (iteration 8) added s-bend jitter without a slalom gain, so the track stays at 0.10 m.
notes: Runnable package: the Builder's body_length 0.11 m on the iteration 10 mass, sensing, drivetrain and controller. Only body_length differs from the best raced design, so the race isolates yaw inertia on the slalom.
rationale: Iteration 10 is the best measured design (785.3, up from 741.9). Its oval finished 20/20 at 1.97 s, its s-bend finished 20/20 with steering_oscillation 0.277 (under the 0.35 limit), and its slalom finished 6/20 with mean progress 0.76, up from 0.68. Yaw inertia is the only geometry lever that has moved the slalom in every step since iteration 7, and the Builder's proposal continues that lever through body_length alone. Body_length 0.12 to 0.11 m lowers yaw inertia by about 8 percent at unchanged mass (0.45 kg), and the contract says body_length has no other dynamic effect. Sensing (seven 12 mm sensors, x = ±0.036 m at 0.012 m pitch, y = 0.06 m), wheel_track 0.10 m, wheel_radius 0.03 m and body_width 0.12 m are unchanged from the best design, so the off-track limit does not move. The controller is kept exactly as in iteration 10 (kp 3.6, kd 0.9, ki 0, base_speed 1.6, last_direction, linear weights -2 to +2), so body_length is the only variable under test. Slalom line loss is still about 1.1 events, so I do not change gains: iteration 8 showed that more turn authority adds s-bend jitter, and iteration 6 showed that a lead change does not help. Expected: slalom progress above 0.76 with more finishes and line loss nearer 1.0, while the oval stays at 20/20 and the s-bend stays at 19/20 or better with steering_oscillation under 0.35. Fallback: if s-bend steering_oscillation exceeds 0.35, the oval loses any trial, or the score falls below 785.3, return body_length to 0.12 m with mass 0.45 kg.
